title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases of Rape and Indecent Assault on Minors

articles.content_en: Article 4 Where rape of a female minor aged fourteen or above or sexual intercourse with a female child under the age of fourteen causes the victim to contract HIV, it shall be deemed as 'causing serious injury to the victim' provided in Item (6) of Paragraph 3 of Article 236 of the Criminal Law.

Article 6 A person with special duties towards a female minor aged fourteen or above who, by taking advantage of a superior position or the victim's isolated and helpless situation, compels the victim to have sexual relations with him, shall be convicted and punished for the crime of rape in accordance with the provisions of Article 236 of the Criminal Law.

Article 9 Coercing or luring a minor to expose intimate body parts or perform obscene acts through online video chat or by sending videos or photos, if meeting the provisions of Article 237 of the Criminal Law, shall be convicted and punished as the crime of compulsory indecency or the crime of indecent assault on a child.
Coercing or luring a minor to perform the acts mentioned in the preceding paragraph through live webcast, if concurrently meeting the provisions of Articles 237 and 365 of the Criminal Law, and constituting the crimes of compulsory indecency, indecent assault on a child, or organizing obscene performances, shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provision that imposes a heavier punishment.

Article 10 Where the commission of a crime of indecent assault on a minor causes the victim to suffer minor injury or above, and concurrently meets the provisions of Article 234 or Article 232 of the Criminal Law, constituting the crime of intentional injury or intentional homicide, the perpetrator shall be convicted and punished in accordance with the provision that imposes a heavier punishment.

Article 11 Where an adult defendant who commits rape or indecent assault on a minor admits guilt and accepts punishment, whether to grant lenient punishment and the extent of leniency shall be strictly controlled.

Article 12 When sentencing an adult defendant who has raped a minor, probation shall generally not be applied.
Where a sentence is imposed and probation is simultaneously declared, a prohibition order may be declared according to the circumstances of the crime, prohibiting the offender from engaging in work or activities related to minors during the probation period, and prohibiting the offender from entering primary and secondary schools, kindergartens, and other places where minors gather. This shall not apply where it is necessary due to the offender's own schooling or residence and with the approval of the enforcement authority.

Article 13 Where a person commits crimes such as rape or indecent assault on a minor by taking advantage of occupational convenience, the People's Court shall apply a prohibition of engagement in certain occupations according to law.

Article 14 Where a person commits crimes such as rape or indecent assault on a minor causing personal injury, compensation shall be paid for reasonable expenses for treatment and rehabilitation, including medical expenses, nursing expenses, transportation expenses, nutritional expenses, hospital meal subsidies, and other such expenses, as well as the loss of income due to missed work.
Expenses required for mental and psychological treatment and rehabilitation of the minor, as proven by expert evaluation opinions, medical diagnosis certificates, or other evidence, shall be deemed as reasonable expenses under the preceding paragraph.

Article 15 'Persons with special duties' as provided in this Interpretation refer to persons who have duties of guardianship, adoption, care, education, medical treatment, or the like towards minors, including persons who have a cohabitation relationship with the minor and in fact have duties of care or protection.
Article 16 This Interpretation shall come into force as of June 1, 2023.
